what is 0153

Service code 0153 = NISD (Not Involving Subdivision).
  • What it is: a straight patta transfer of the whole survey number — no new sub-division is created, so no field visit and no SD sketch.
  • Workflow: Citizen / CSC / Sub-Registrar → SIS (document verification) → Zonal Level Tahsildar (DSC signature, order generated).
  • Fee: Government ₹100.00 + CSC charge ₹60.00.
  • SLA: 15-20 working days.
  • Field visit: not required.

what is 0154

Service code 0154 = ISD (Involving Subdivision).
  • What it is: a patta transfer in which the parcel is split, so a field inspection and a sub-division sketch are required.
  • Workflow: Citizen / CSC / Sub-Registrar → SIS (mandatory field visit) → Senior Draughtsman (SD sketch) → DIS → Tahsildar (DSC).
  • Fee: Government ₹400.00 + CSC charge ₹60.00.
  • SLA: 30-35 working days.
  • Field visit: required.

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. Every application carries one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

What does the SIS guide say about ownership record: what is held per owner?

Ownership of a survey number / sub-division is held as one row per owner, so a
jointly held parcel simply has several owner rows. For each owner the register
keeps: name (English and Tamil), the father's / husband's name with the
relationship (s/o, w/o, d/o), gender, address, the last four digits of the
Aadhaar number, and the ownership share. Two or more owner rows on the same
survey number means the parcel is jointly owned; a single row means a sole
owner.

The register does NOT hold an owner's mobile number, ration card number,
voter ID (EPIC), PIN code, occupation code or door number - those columns are
blank in the source extracts and are not projected. A question about one of
them is answered as "not recorded", not treated as missing data.

  Total: 800 + 900 = 1700 sq.m ✗ INVALID (Missing 300 sq.m)

- All areas recorded in square meters (sq.m)
- Minimum measurable area: 1 sq.m
- Maximum precision: 2 decimal places (e.g., 456.75 sq.m)
- Survey measurements must be verified in field

- Example: 1000 sq.m survey can have 995-1005 sq.m total

What does the SIS guide say about merge rules: which sub-divisions can be merged?

Survey Number Merging:
- Combines multiple survey numbers or sub-divisions into single survey number
- Used when adjacent land parcels are purchased by same owner
- Simplifies land records and patta management

Merge Eligibility Criteria:

1. Common Ownership
   - All survey numbers must have same owner
   - Ownership must be sole (not joint) or all joint owners must agree
   - Patta holder name must match across all surveys

2. Geographic Adjacency
   - Survey numbers must share common boundary
   - Non-adjacent surveys cannot be merged
   - At least one common boundary point required

3. Same Jurisdiction
   - All surveys must belong to same block
   - Surveys from different blocks cannot be merged
   - Surveys must be in same ward and town

4. Same Land Classification
   - All surveys must have same land type (agricultural, residential, commercial)
